recentItems.title: Weapons & the Law (S7 E4)
recentItems.description:
The Canadian Army is accelerating its modernization — introducing new weapons and technologies to meet emerging threats. But before anything is bought or fired, a critical step must be taken: ensuring it’s actually legal to use. 

Major Michael Smith is a Canadian Armed Forces legal officer with the Directorate of International Operational Law. He explains how international humanitarian law shapes the weapons Canada develops, acquires, and uses. Find out why some weapons are banned, how others can be used legally or illegally depending on context, and how Canada works to keep warfare within the bounds of humanity — even as technology evolves.

recentItems.title: Ex OREGON TRAIL
recentItems.description:
From 12–27 June 2026, soldiers from The Royal Westminster Regiment participated in Exercise OREGON TRAIL, conducting training at Yakima Training Center (YTC) and Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM),Washington, alongside the Oregon National Guard's 41st Infantry Brigade Combat Team (IBCT).

The two-week exercise strengthened interoperability with U.S. partners through a demanding series of tactical training events conducted across both YTC/JBLM. Soldiers participated in live-fire platoon attacks, close quarters battle (CQB), familiarization with U.S. weapon systems, helicopter insertions, amphibious assaults, and helo-casting operations. CQB training was conducted with the U.S. Army's 1st Special Forces Group (Airborne), providing valuable experience in advanced close-quarters tactics and techniques. Exercises such as OREGON TRAIL enhance combat readiness while reinforcing the enduring partnership between the Canadian Armed Forces and the U.S Army.

Video by: Cpl Su, The Seaforth Highlanders of Canada
Edited by:Cpl Su, Pte Del Castillo Berrera

recentItems.title: EOD Operator | Explosive Ordnance Disposal (S7 E3)
recentItems.description:
The battlefield is saturated with explosives—from factory‑made munitions and improvised bombs to drones delivering lethal payloads. At the same time, unexploded ordnance from past wars may still lie hidden beneath the ground. Neutralizing these threats is essential to keeping troops moving and civilians safe. This is where Explosive Ordnance Disposal Operators like Master Warrant Officer Marty Gratrix come in. He offers an inside look at a career spent defusing danger with no room for error.
